zh.summary: 分清技術嚴重度、已知利用與未來機率，以適用性、可達性及後果安排修補。

sourceBody.text: 一、先理解：最嚴重的漏洞，不一定最需要先修
這堂課最重要的觀念是：
漏洞有多嚴重、駭客有沒有利用、你的系統有多危險，是三個不同的問題。
假設你是公司的資安工程師，今天掃描出 100 個漏洞，但是只有時間修補其中 10 個。
你會怎麼選？
可能有人說：「從 CVSS 分數最高的開始修就好了！」
問題是，有些 9.8 分的漏洞可能只存在於完全隔離的實驗室；某個 8.1 分的漏洞卻可能存在於公司對外服務的伺服器，而且駭客已經在利用這個漏洞攻擊其他企業。
這時候，後者反而更值得優先處理。
我們需要三種工具協助判斷：
CVSS — 漏洞有多嚴重？
好比門鎖的設計缺陷有多嚴重，以及被突破後可能有什麼後果。
KEV — 駭客真的利用過嗎？
好比已經有可靠消息確認，竊賊正在利用這種門鎖缺陷作案。
EPSS — 接下來被利用的可能性有多高？
好比根據過去案例與目前跡象，預測未來 30 天這類缺陷被用來作案的可能性。

visual.caption: 圖 1｜三種工具，三個問題
visual.description: 三項平行訊號：技術嚴重度、已知利用與未來利用機率；仍需本地資產情境。

items.title: CVSS — 漏洞有多嚴重？
items.body: 好比門鎖的設計缺陷有多嚴重，以及被突破後可能有什麼後果。

items.title: KEV — 駭客真的利用過嗎？
items.body: 好比已經有可靠消息確認，竊賊正在利用這種門鎖缺陷作案。

items.title: EPSS — 接下來被利用的可能性有多高？
items.body: 好比根據過去案例與目前跡象，預測未來 30 天這類缺陷被用來作案的可能性。

sourceBody.text: 但這三個工具都不知道你的完整公司環境。因此還需要第四個問題：
這個漏洞真的影響我的哪一台設備？這台設備有多重要、是否容易被攻擊？
這才是 Vulnerability Prioritization（漏洞處理優先順序）的核心。
二、CVSS：告訴你漏洞有多嚴重
CVSS 全名是 Common Vulnerability Scoring System，中文是「通用漏洞評分系統」。
你可以把它當成漏洞的技術危險程度評量表。
這是 CVSS 的標準嚴重度分級。 [FIRST CVSS v4.0 規範](https://www.first.org/cvss/v4.0/specification-document)
例如，假設某個漏洞是 CVSS 9.8 分。
它的意思不是「有 98% 的機率被駭」。
它是在說，根據這個版本、評分類型與向量所描述的技術條件，這是一個非常嚴重的漏洞。
CVSS 主要評估什麼？
想像駭客要利用一台伺服器的漏洞：

items: Attack Vector（攻擊途徑）： 能不能從網路上攻擊？還是必須接觸設備？
Attack Complexity（攻擊複雜度）： 攻擊成功需要克服多少技術障礙？
Privileges Required（所需權限）： 是否需要先取得帳號或管理權限？
User Interaction（使用者互動）： 是否需要有人點擊、開啟檔案或進行其他操作？
Impact（影響）： 成功後能否偷資料、竄改資料或使系統停止運作？

sourceBody.text: CVSS v4.0 的 Base 指標還包含 Attack Requirements（攻擊必要條件），並區分受漏洞影響的系統與後續受影響系統。 [FIRST CVSS v4.0 規範](https://www.first.org/cvss/v4.0/specification-document)
CVSS v4.0 的四個層次
Base（基本）
漏洞本身具備什麼技術特性？可能造成什麼後果？
Threat（威脅）
是否已出現可用的利用技術，或實際利用活動？
Environmental（環境）
放到我的公司後，系統的重要性、防護與實際條件有什麼差別？
Supplemental（補充）
還有什麼額外資訊值得參考，例如復原困難程度？這組指標不改變 CVSS 分數。

visual.caption: 圖 2｜CVSS v4.0 的四組指標
visual.description: 四組指標的用途不同；Supplemental 不改變分數。上下排列用於閱讀，不表示先後流程。

items.title: Base（基本）
items.body: 漏洞本身具備什麼技術特性？可能造成什麼後果？

items.title: Threat（威脅）
items.body: 是否已出現可用的利用技術，或實際利用活動？

items.title: Environmental（環境）
items.body: 放到我的公司後，系統的重要性、防護與實際條件有什麼差別？

items.title: Supplemental（補充）
items.body: 還有什麼額外資訊值得參考，例如復原困難程度？這組指標不改變 CVSS 分數。

sourceBody.text: 這代表 CVSS 不只是公告上常看到的 Base Score。它還能結合威脅與環境資訊，讓技術嚴重度評估更符合實際部署情境，但仍不能取代完整的業務風險分析。 [FIRST CVSS v4.0 規範](https://www.first.org/cvss/v4.0/specification-document)
這一節最重要的結論：CVSS 很高，代表值得重視；但不能只憑 CVSS 決定修補先後。
三、KEV：這個漏洞真的被駭客利用過嗎？
KEV 是 Known Exploited Vulnerabilities，也就是「已知遭利用漏洞目錄」，由美國 CISA 維護。
假設你看到兩則公告：

items: 漏洞 A：研究人員發現，可以利用某個錯誤取得管理員權限。
漏洞 B：研究人員發現同樣的問題，而且已經有可靠證據顯示攻擊者在真實環境中利用它。

sourceBody.text: 兩個漏洞都嚴重，但 B 多了一項重要的威脅證據。
這就是 KEV 的價值。
要注意，研究人員公開 PoC（概念驗證程式），不等於漏洞已在真實攻擊中被利用。 CISA 的 KEV 收錄標準要求有實際利用證據，單純掃描或安全研究並不足以成立。 [CISA 官方 KEV 公告與收錄條件](https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/USDHSCISA/bulletins/42a9f71)
如果漏洞列入 KEV，我該怎麼做？
先區分三個判斷：

rows: 已有外部實際利用證據
需要核對版本、設定與影響條件
需要日誌、系統跡證或其他調查證據

sourceBody.text: 這三件事不能畫上等號。
例如，公司使用的防火牆存在 KEV 漏洞，代表應該提高處理優先順序，必要時調查是否存在入侵跡證，但不能直接向主管宣布「公司已經被駭」。
同樣地，沒有列入 KEV，也不能保證攻擊者沒有利用這個漏洞。
四、EPSS：預測未來 30 天被利用的可能性
EPSS 是 Exploit Prediction Scoring System，由 FIRST 提供。
它運用機器學習與漏洞相關的威脅訊號，估計特定 CVE 在未來 30 天被觀察到真實利用活動的機率，而且每天更新。 [FIRST EPSS](https://www.first.org/epss/)
例如，你看到：
假設某漏洞的 EPSS
代表模型預測，這個 CVE 在接下來 30 天於其觀測範圍內出現利用活動的機率約為 20%。
這是全球漏洞層級的預測，不是你的單一伺服器有 20% 的機率遭到入侵。

visual.caption: 圖 3｜假設某漏洞的 EPSS
visual.description: 固定教學數值。藍色長條佔全長 20%，不表示修補進度或本機遭入侵的機率。

items.body:
代表模型預測，這個 CVE 在接下來 30 天於其觀測範圍內出現利用活動的機率約為 20%。

這是全球漏洞層級的預測，不是你的單一伺服器有 20% 的機率遭到入侵。

sourceBody.text: EPSS 的兩個欄位最容易搞混

rows: 未來 30 天利用機率預測為 20%
分數高於約 95% 的受評漏洞

sourceBody.text: 這兩個數值只是說明用途的假設範例，並非同一筆實際評分。
Probability 是預測機率；Percentile 則是相對排名。不能把第 95 百分位解讀成 95% 被利用機率。 [FIRST Probability 與 Percentile 說明](https://www.first.org/epss/articles/prob_percentile_bins)
更重要的是，EPSS 不知道你公司的系統是否連上網際網路、是否有防火牆保護，或者裡面存放什麼資料。
另外，EPSS 為 1% 也不代表風險等於零。若已經有 KEV 等可靠實際利用證據，應優先考慮這些證據，而不是因為 EPSS 低就忽略。 [FIRST EPSS 實務指南](https://www.first.org/epss/using-epss)
五、真正的排序方法：四個問題依序回答
這裡給你一套可以用於真實資安工作的決策流程。
第一關：漏洞是否真的影響我的資產？
確認產品、版本、設定、受影響功能
第二關：漏洞與外部威脅訊號告訴我什麼？
CVSS、KEV、EPSS 及其他威脅情資
此處 CVSS 提供技術嚴重度背景，分數本身不是外部實際利用的證據；KEV 與 EPSS 分別回答不同的威脅問題。
第三關：攻擊者能接近嗎？影響多大？
網路曝露、權限、防護、資料與業務重要性
第四關：決定處理優先順序與措施
立即緩解、安排修補、驗證、持續追蹤

visual.description: 箭頭表示定性判斷順序；這不是官方計分公式。CVSS 提供嚴重度，KEV／EPSS 補充不同威脅訊號。

items.title: 第一關：漏洞是否真的影響我的資產？
items.body: 確認產品、版本、設定、受影響功能

items.title: 第二關：漏洞與外部威脅訊號告訴我什麼？
items.body: CVSS、KEV、EPSS 及其他威脅情資

items.title: 第三關：攻擊者能接近嗎？影響多大？
items.body: 網路曝露、權限、防護、資料與業務重要性

items.title: 第四關：決定處理優先順序與措施
items.body: 立即緩解、安排修補、驗證、持續追蹤

sourceBody.text: 這是一種定性的風險決策流程，不是官方提供的自動計分公式。
實際執行時，我建議特別注意三個因素：
Presence（存在性）： 你的系統是否真的受影響？
Reachability（可達性）： 攻擊者是否具備接觸與利用漏洞的必要條件？
Consequence（後果）： 如果成功利用，會造成多嚴重的業務或安全影響？
FIRST 的 EPSS 實務指南也強調，應將這三種本地情境與漏洞利用預測結合。 [FIRST EPSS 實務指南](https://www.first.org/epss/using-epss)
六、實際案例：CVSS 9.8 與 8.1，你會先修誰？
以下都是虛構的教學數據。
單看 CVSS，你可能選甲。
但如果你同時考慮外部威脅與實際環境，應該優先處理乙。
原因不是 8.1 比 9.8 嚴重，而是乙同時符合幾個條件：已有實際利用證據、可從外部接觸、設備具備重要業務功能，而且漏洞尚未修復。
相對而言，甲雖然技術嚴重度較高，但目前有經過驗證的隔離措施，且業務影響較低，因此可以在可接受的風險與政策期限內安排後續修補。
但是，如果後來發現甲的隔離設定失效，或乙已有經過確認且有效的緩解措施，優先順序就必須重新評估。
排序之後還要做什麼？
決定乙優先，不代表立即在正式環境安裝更新、強制重新開機。
你仍然需要判斷：

items: 能否先以限制網路入口、停用受影響功能或原廠建議措施降低曝露？
更新會不會造成服務中斷？是否需要測試與回復方案？
修補後要用什麼證據確認漏洞已解除、系統仍正常運作？
如果已知存在攻擊活動，是否需要額外檢查本機入侵跡證？

sourceBody.text: 要特別分清楚：已完成緩解，不一定代表已修復；已安裝更新，也不一定代表已驗證安全。
七、給實務工作的一份簡單紀錄表
你可以把這張表用於弱點掃描結果、滲透測試後續處置或日常漏洞管理。

rows: 先緩解，再依核准程序修補
版本、設定、重新掃描與功能測試結果

sourceBody.text: 正式紀錄還要加上資訊來源、負責人、處理期限、核准及例外紀錄。
官方資料可以從這幾個入口取得：

items: [FIRST CVSS v4.0：規範與計分工具](https://www.first.org/cvss/v4.0/)
[CISA KEV：已知遭利用漏洞目錄](https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog)
[FIRST EPSS：利用機率查詢與資料下載](https://www.first.org/epss/)

sourceBody.text: 提醒：CISA 於 2026 年發布的 BOD 26-04 針對美國聯邦文職行政機關訂有風險導向的漏洞管理要求，不能未經核對就把其中要求當成臺灣私人企業的法定期限。 [CISA 官方發布公告](https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/USDHSCISA/bulletins/41b445a)與[適用範圍說明](https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/USDHSCISA/bulletins/4309083)
八、學完這堂課，你應該帶走什麼？
CVSS、KEV、EPSS 最容易記憶的方式是：
CVSS 衡量技術嚴重度；KEV 提供已知實際利用證據；EPSS 預測未來 30 天的利用活動機率。
真正的修補優先順序則要看：
漏洞是否適用 + 攻擊者是否容易接近 + 外部威脅證據 + 成功利用的後果 + 現有防護。
因此，不要只按照 CVSS 由高到低排序，也不要把 CVSS、KEV、EPSS 隨意加權，誤以為得到一個官方認證的風險分數。
九、理解檢核
假設你是資安工程師，同事告訴你：
這個漏洞 CVSS 9.8，但 EPSS 只有 1%，而且沒有列入 KEV。所以我們完全不需要處理它。
請回答兩個問題：

items: 這位同事的結論缺少哪兩類最重要的本地環境證據？
假設漏洞存在於公司內部的關鍵資料庫，而不是對外網站，你會直接降低它的修補優先順序嗎？為什麼？

sourceBody.text: 請用白話文回答，核對推理是否連結漏洞適用性、可達性與後果，不只背誦定義。

en.summary: Separate technical severity, known exploitation and predicted likelihood; prioritize remediation using applicability, reachability and consequences.

sourceBody.text: 1. Start here: the most severe vulnerability may not be the first to fix
The central idea of this lesson is:
How severe a vulnerability is, whether attackers have exploited it, and how much danger your system faces are three different questions.
Imagine you are a security engineer. Today's scan finds 100 vulnerabilities, but you only have time to remediate 10.
How would you choose?
Someone might say, “Just start with the highest CVSS score!”

The difficulty is that a vulnerability rated 9.8 might exist only in a fully isolated laboratory. Another rated 8.1 might affect an internet-facing company server, and attackers might already be exploiting it against other organizations.
In that situation, the latter deserves attention first.
Three tools help us judge:
CVSS — How severe is the vulnerability?
Think of the seriousness of a lock's design flaw and the possible consequences of defeating it.
KEV — Have attackers actually exploited it?
Think of reliable reports confirming that burglars are using this type of lock defect in real crimes.
EPSS — How likely is exploitation in the near future?
Think of using past cases and current signals to predict the likelihood that this kind of defect will be used in the next 30 days.

visual.caption: Figure 1 | Three tools, three questions
visual.description: Parallel signals: technical severity, known exploitation and predicted exploitation. Local asset context is still required.

items.title: CVSS — How severe is it?
items.body: Like assessing a lock's design defect and the consequences of defeating it.

items.title: KEV — Has it actually been exploited?
items.body: Like reliable reports confirming burglars using this lock defect in real crimes.

items.title: EPSS — How likely is exploitation next?
items.body: Like predicting use of this defect in the next 30 days from past cases and current signals.

sourceBody.text: None of these tools knows your complete company environment. A fourth question is needed:
Which of my devices does this vulnerability actually affect? How important is that device, and how accessible is it to an attacker?
This is the core of vulnerability prioritization: deciding the order in which to address vulnerabilities.
2. CVSS: how severe is the vulnerability?
CVSS stands for Common Vulnerability Scoring System.
Think of it as an assessment of a vulnerability's technical severity.
These are the standard CVSS qualitative severity bands. [FIRST CVSS v4.0 specification](https://www.first.org/cvss/v4.0/specification-document)
For example, suppose a vulnerability has a CVSS score of 9.8.
That does not mean a “98% chance of being hacked.”
It means the vulnerability is very severe under the technical conditions described by that version, metric combination and vector.
What does CVSS mainly assess?
Imagine an attacker trying to exploit a server vulnerability:

items: Attack Vector: Can the attack come over a network, or must the attacker physically touch the device?
Attack Complexity: What technical obstacles must the attacker overcome to succeed?
Privileges Required: Does the attacker need an account or administrative privileges first?
User Interaction: Must someone click, open a file or take another action?
Impact: Could successful exploitation steal data, change data or stop the system from working?

sourceBody.text: CVSS v4.0 Base metrics also include Attack Requirements and distinguish impacts on the vulnerable system from impacts on subsequent systems. [FIRST CVSS v4.0 specification](https://www.first.org/cvss/v4.0/specification-document)
The four CVSS v4.0 metric groups
Base
What intrinsic technical characteristics does the vulnerability have? What consequences could it cause?
Threat
Are exploitation techniques available, or has exploitation activity occurred?
Environmental
In my company, how do system importance, defenses and actual deployment conditions differ?
Supplemental
What additional information matters, such as recovery difficulty? These metrics do not change the CVSS score.

visual.caption: Figure 2 | Four CVSS v4.0 metric groups
visual.description: Each group has a different purpose. Supplemental does not change the score. Rows are for reading, not a sequence.

items.title: Base
items.body: What intrinsic technical characteristics and possible consequences does the vulnerability have?

items.title: Threat
items.body: Are exploitation techniques available, or has exploitation activity occurred?

items.title: Environmental
items.body: How do system importance, defenses and actual conditions differ in my company?

items.title: Supplemental
items.body: What else matters, such as recovery difficulty? These metrics do not change the CVSS score.

sourceBody.text: CVSS therefore includes more than the Base Score commonly shown in advisories. Threat and environmental information can refine the technical severity assessment for an actual deployment, while a complete business risk analysis still requires more information. [FIRST CVSS v4.0 specification](https://www.first.org/cvss/v4.0/specification-document)
The main conclusion of this section: a high CVSS score deserves attention, but CVSS alone cannot decide remediation order.
3. KEV: has this vulnerability actually been exploited?
KEV stands for Known Exploited Vulnerabilities. CISA maintains this catalog.
Suppose you see two advisories:

items: Vulnerability A: Researchers discovered that a particular error can be used to gain administrator privileges.
Vulnerability B: Researchers discovered the same kind of problem, and reliable evidence shows attackers exploiting it in real environments.

sourceBody.text: Both vulnerabilities are serious, but B has an additional piece of threat evidence.
That is the value of KEV.

A published PoC, or proof-of-concept program, is different from evidence of exploitation in real attacks. KEV inclusion requires exploitation evidence; scanning alone or security research does not establish that evidence. [CISA official KEV bulletin and inclusion criteria](https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/USDHSCISA/bulletins/42a9f71)
What should I do if a vulnerability is in KEV?
Separate three judgments first:

rows: Does my device have this vulnerability?
Check versions, configuration and affected conditions
Investigate logs, system artifacts or other incident evidence

sourceBody.text: These are three separate conclusions.

For example, a KEV vulnerability affecting a company firewall warrants higher remediation priority and, where appropriate, investigation for intrusion artifacts. It does not by itself support telling management, “Our company has been hacked.”
Likewise, absence from KEV does not establish that attackers have never exploited the vulnerability.
4. EPSS: predicting exploitation in the next 30 days
EPSS stands for Exploit Prediction Scoring System and is provided by FIRST.

It uses machine learning and vulnerability-related threat signals to estimate the probability of observing exploitation of a specific CVE in the wild in the next 30 days. Scores are updated daily. [FIRST EPSS](https://www.first.org/epss/)
For example, you might see:
Suppose a vulnerability has an EPSS score of
The model predicts about a 20% probability of observing exploitation activity for this CVE in the next 30 days within its observation scope.
This is a prediction at the global vulnerability level. It is not a 20% probability that your individual server will be compromised.

sourceBody.text: The two EPSS fields that are easy to confuse

rows: Predicted probability of exploitation in the next 30 days: 20%
A score higher than approximately 95% of assessed vulnerabilities

sourceBody.text: These are hypothetical examples for explanation, not two fields from one actual assessment.

Probability is the predicted likelihood; percentile is a relative ranking. The 95th percentile must not be read as a 95% exploitation probability. [FIRST probability and percentile explanation](https://www.first.org/epss/articles/prob_percentile_bins)
EPSS also does not know whether your company's system is internet-connected, protected by a firewall or holding particular data.

An EPSS value of 1% does not make the risk zero. When reliable evidence of exploitation exists, such as KEV inclusion, prioritize that evidence rather than dismissing the vulnerability because EPSS is low. [FIRST using EPSS](https://www.first.org/epss/using-epss)
5. A practical ordering method: answer four questions in sequence
Here is a decision process for vulnerability management work.
First gate: Does the vulnerability actually affect my asset?
Confirm the product, version, configuration and affected feature.
Second gate: What do the vulnerability and external threat signals tell us?
CVSS, KEV, EPSS and other threat intelligence.
CVSS contributes technical severity context here; the score alone is not evidence of external exploitation. KEV and EPSS answer different threat questions.
Third gate: Can an attacker reach it, and what would the impact be?
Network exposure, privileges, defenses, data and business importance.
Fourth gate: Decide the remediation priority and measures.
Immediate mitigation, scheduled patching, verification and continued tracking.

sourceBody.text: This is a qualitative risk decision process, not an official automatic scoring formula.
In practice, pay particular attention to three factors:
Presence: Is your system actually affected?
Reachability: Does an attacker have the conditions needed to reach and exploit the vulnerability?
Consequence: How serious would the business or safety impact be if exploitation succeeded?
FIRST's practical EPSS guidance also emphasizes combining this local context with exploitation predictions. [FIRST using EPSS](https://www.first.org/epss/using-epss)
6. A worked example: CVSS 9.8 versus 8.1 — which comes first?
All values below are fictional teaching data.
Looking only at CVSS, you might choose A.
Considering external threats and the actual environment together, B should be addressed first.
This does not mean that 8.1 is more severe than 9.8. B combines evidence of exploitation, external accessibility, an important business role and an unremediated vulnerability.
A has higher technical severity, but its isolation has been verified and its business impact is lower. Remediation can therefore be scheduled within acceptable risk and applicable policy deadlines.
If A's isolation later proves ineffective, or B has a confirmed effective mitigation, reassess the priority.
What comes after prioritization?
Deciding that B comes first does not mean immediately installing an update and forcing a reboot in production.
You still need to judge:

items: Can you reduce exposure first by restricting network entry points, disabling the affected feature or applying vendor-recommended measures?
Could the update interrupt the service? Do you need testing and a rollback plan?
What evidence will confirm that the vulnerability is resolved and the system still works after remediation?
If attack activity is known, should you also investigate local intrusion artifacts?

sourceBody.text: Keep the states distinct: mitigation can be complete while the vulnerability remains unpatched; installing an update still requires verification that the remediation worked.

8. What should you take away?
A useful way to remember CVSS, KEV and EPSS is:
CVSS measures technical severity; KEV supplies evidence of known exploitation; EPSS predicts the probability of exploitation activity in the next 30 days.
Actual remediation priority also depends on:
Applicability + attacker reachability + external threat evidence + the consequences of successful exploitation + existing defenses.
Avoid sorting solely by descending CVSS. Arbitrarily weighting CVSS, KEV and EPSS together does not produce an officially certified risk score.
9. Check your understanding
Imagine you are a security engineer and a colleague tells you:
“This vulnerability has CVSS 9.8, but EPSS is only 1%, and it is not in KEV. We do not need to do anything about it.”
Answer two questions:

items: Which two important categories of local environmental evidence are missing from this conclusion?
If the vulnerability affects a critical internal company database instead of an external website, would you automatically lower its remediation priority? Why?

sourceBody.text: Answer in plain language. Check whether your reasoning connects applicability, reachability and consequences; memorizing definitions alone is insufficient.
